main_text.l: mus, abhinc annos quinque & quadrin-ginta, Arbitrone & Lolliano consuli-bus, Sed Liberius paulo post urbi reddi-tur, ob ieditiones[?] Romanas. Ceterumexules latis cōstat totius orbis studiis ce-lebratos, pecuniaq; eis infumptum af-fatim congestas, legationibus quoq; cosplebis catholicae, ex omnibus fere pro-vinciis frequetatos. Interea Arriani nonocculte, ut antea, sed palam ac publice haeresis piacula praedicabant: quin etiam synodum Nicenam pro se interpretates, quam unius litera adjectione corrupe-rant, caliginem quandam injecerant ve-ritati. Nam ubi ὁμοούσιον[?] erat scriptū, quodunius est substantiae: illi ὁμοιούσιον[?], quod estsimilis substantiae, scriptum esse dicebat: coccedentes similitudinem, dum adime-rent unitatem: quia multum ab unitate similitudo distaret. ut, verbi gratia, pictu-ra humani corporis esset homini similis, nec tamen haberet hominis {b}veritatem. Sed quidam ex his ultra processerant, A-nomoeousiam, id est, dissimilem substantiam confirmantes. page.notes: The text is a 16th/17th-century Latin page with Greek words. The marginal notes are on the left and are transcribed as printed, with hyphens kept where they break across lines. The note marked "b" is the note "vnita-tem, Sigo." beside "veritatem" (I have placed the mark in the text). Uncertain readings: "ieditiones" (possibly a misprint), the two Greek words (ὁμοούσιον and ὁμοιούσιον), and the page number "152", which is hard to read. The running head is taken from the printed "SVLPICII SEVERI" heading. The "b" note text was partly obscured, so "vnita-tem, Sigo." is uncertain. The text of the notes on the left margin ("a Secundo", "dorelus lib.2.cap.", "An.357", "Conc.Ni-", "cæni de-", "pravatio.") may be incomplete or misaligned with the lines.
